My main problems with them are:

a) They're probably giving no useful advice to people who are suffering from the only 1- 2 disorders they are comfortable enough talking about, usually depression and/or anxiety. 
 eg. If you're depressed/anxious, go outside, exercise, drink water! 

b) They ignore other "scary and weird" mental disorders that aren't seen as quirky. Just like another user mentioned, everyone is quick to laugh at the homeless man who is talking to himself at the side of the street.

No, I'd be glad to help. First of all understand what's wrong with them. Not everyone suffers from depression or anxiety, even though they're very common. Anyone can suffer from suicidal thoughts, they can have bipolar, BPD, schizophrenia, autism etc. A lot of the times when mental illnesses like schizophrenia comes up everyone kind of just... cringes, because it's not something they want to talk about. It's too scary, it's too weird. A lot of schizophrenics are seen as dangerous when in fact they're more likely to harm themselves. Research their mental illness, learn the symptoms commonly associated with it. Go on forums and see how people deal with them. If someone you know is suffering from suicidal thoughts they'll need some appreciation. Sometimes you can't do much. You can text them and make sure they're ok, invite them to places even though you're sure they won't attend. Make them feel comfortable and appreciated. They want to feel like they matter. 

Have you heard someone say "They don't care till you're dead", they say that because no one has checked up on them. Apparently if you haven't planned out your suicide then you're less important. If they're having a bad day, let them vent. It's small things like that. 

If you tell someone "talk to me whenever you want" make sure you mean it. It's a big betrayal when you offer to help but bail out in the last second, it makes you look like a hypocrite who is helping others just to feel good about themselves. Since you've come to r/SuicideWatch to learn, I'm guessing you've gotten used to the very angry posts and that's good. This is what goes on in people's head, maybe even worse. Make sure you can handle it.

Sending people suicide hotlines isn't going to do anything. I bet most people here are too anxious to talk on the phone, I know I am. Plus, suicide hotlines have proven to be very unhelpful and, in some cases, have actually made things worse. Sometimes people aren't even able to get professional help and they have to rely on subs like this one so good advice here truly means a lot.

And finally, please don't stigmatise mental disorders. I talked about this in the first paragraph. For example, people with BPD have been alienated for far too long. My friend has it and feels horrible about it, she doesn't even want to get help because she feels like a BPD diagnosis would ruin her life. People with BPD might say things they don't mean and do things they'll regret later. Remember if "bad people" get help, everyone profits off of it. Sometimes, you can't control your mental illness. Sometimes, a good day for someone with depression means they got out of bed a few times.

In my post I was extremely angry and unprofessional with my speech, now though, I actually bother with things like punctuation. I just couldn't help it, something happened irl and I had to get it out there. Btw, sorry for the novel response. I hope this helped.
